Normal values

  • Total serum bilirubin 8.5–20.5 µmol/L; of this, indirect (free) ~75%, direct (conjugated) ~25%.
  • Jaundice becomes visible when bilirubin exceeds ~30–35 µmol/L.

Differential diagnosis of jaundice

  • Hemolytic: ↑ indirect; urine — ↑ urobilin, no bilirubin; stool dark.
  • Hepatic: ↑ direct and indirect; urine — bilirubin and urobilin; stool lighter; ↑ ALT, AST.
  • Obstructive: ↑↑ direct; urine — bilirubin, no urobilin; stool acholic; ↑ alkaline phosphatase, cholesterol, bile acids.

Inherited hyperbilirubinemias

Gilbert (reduced conjugation, mild), Crigler–Najjar (almost no UDP-glucuronosyltransferase, severe), Dubin–Johnson and Rotor (impaired excretion of direct bilirubin).

Models

  • Heme uses real coordinates from oxyhemoglobin (PDB 1GZX); protoporphyrin IX is the same ring without iron.
  • Hydroxymethylbilane, uroporphyrinogen III and coproporphyrinogen III (non-aromatic rings with CH₂ bridges, with 8 and 4 carboxyl groups), biliverdin, bilirubin, porphobilinogen, ALA and glucuronic acid are built from their chemical formulas.
  • Bilirubin values for the types of jaundice are typical examples, not cutoffs.
